entries.notes: Two edits, at the entry's two printed sites: l.196 (a pointer, marker l.197) and a sentence inserted after l.231 (now l.232, marker l.233; v1 printed l.231-234). In words, l.232 says: for an EGF (pi = sum alpha^i delta_{Phi_i}), if F_out << lambda and (Phi_i)_# lambda << lambda for every i, then F_in = sum_i (Phi_i)_#(alpha^i F_out) << lambda, and so f_in = dF_in/dlambda exists (lambda finite). The Lean says: EGF.inflow_ac_of_map_ac and EGF.InflowAC.of_map_ac hold on any measurable space and for any lambda. They take IsEGFPolicy (Phi_i measurable, no inverse; alpha measurable, >= 0, summing to 1; pi = sum alpha delta_Phi), hPhi : lam.map (Phi i) << lam and hout : F_out << lam, and conclude inflow << lam. EGF.inflow_eq_withDensity_of_map_ac adds [SigmaFinite lam] and F_out finite, and concludes F_in = (sum_i d((Phi_i)_#(alpha^i F_out))/dlam) lam. Hypothesis by hypothesis. IsEGFPolicy is the EGF definition (l.218-222) with pi Markov (l.161). hPhi is the added hypothesis, and it is stated: (Phi_i)_# mu := mu(Phi_i^{-1}(.)) is Measure.map, so the TeX's (Phi_i)_# lambda << lambda is hPhi literally. hout is stated explicitly. It is also presupposed by the density f_out (l.194, l.199, l.744), so it adds no restriction. sigma-finite lambda is supplied by '(lambda being finite)' and l.161; that is stronger than needed (finding 1). F_out finite comes from l.161. Conclusions. 'F_in << lambda' is inflow_ac_of_map_ac. 'f_in exists' is inflow_eq_withDensity_of_map_ac. The displayed identity F_in = sum_i (Phi_i)_#(alpha^i F_out) is EGF.IsEGFPolicy.inflow_eq_sum_map, which is proved but not a listed anchor (finding 3). The l.196 pointer ('the latter presupposes F_in << lambda, which holds for an EGF since its moves are nonsingular (Section 3)') makes the same claim; F_out << lambda is implicit there in the f_out of l.194, and the forward reference resolves to l.232. The instance '(true for diffeomorphisms and the Riemannian volume)' is proved in its Euclidean case (C^n diffeomorphisms with Haar/Lebesgue measure, EGF.map_ac_of_diffeomorph, not listed) and not formalized in its Riemannian case (finding 2). Kind missing-hypothesis, so there is no refutation to answer. The C-7 refutation instance (printed_inflow_not_ac) violates the added hypothesis (EGF.not_map_ac_acMap), so it is excluded here as well. pinsker_negative_control_nonsingular backs the consequence for Corollary 3.10 (InflowAC discharged for an EGF); the TeX states nothing new there. added_hypotheses lists '(Phi_i)_# lambda << lambda', which is at l.232 and, as 'its moves are nonsingular', at l.196. No hypothesis restricting the paper was added beyond it.

l.743 replaces 'lambda absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure' by 'lambda for which every Phi_i is nonsingular, (Phi_i)_# lambda << lambda (for instance the Riemannian volume, or any lambda equivalent to Lebesgue measure)'. With C-8 and C-9, the theorem (l.746-756) now reads as follows. Setting: a differential manifold with lambda; Phi_i diffeomorphisms with (Phi_i)_# lambda << lambda; a generative flow with F_out = f_out lambda and pi(s) = sum alpha^i(s) delta_{Phi_i(s)}. Then (1) f_in = sum_j (alpha^j f_out) o Phi_j^{-1} J^lambda_j. (2) B* = sum beta^i delta_{Phi_i^{-1}}, with beta^i = (alpha^i f_out) o Phi_i^{-1} J^lambda_i / f_in, is a backward star policy. (3) beta^i is defined F_in-a.e. (4) The backward policy is unique setwise, F_in-a.e. Against EGF.backward_policy_rnDeriv, hypothesis by hypothesis. [SigmaFinite lam] comes from l.161's finite lambda (the two examples are sigma-finite too). F : GenerativeFlow (pi Markov, F_out finite) is l.161. Phi_i : S ≃ᵐ S is weaker than the TeX's diffeomorphisms. hac : (Phi_i)_# lambda << lambda is stated (the added hypothesis). IsEGFPolicy is l.744 with the policy alpha in [0,1]^p of l.222. f_out measurable and hout (F_out = f_out lambda) are l.744. Every Lean hypothesis is therefore in the TeX or in its setting. The dropped 'lambda << Lebesgue' is not needed (the Lean works on any measurable space). Conclusions: (1) is conjunct 1, (2) is conjunct 2, (3) is conjunct 3 plus the definition of backwardWeight, and (4) is conjunct 4. The TeX claims nothing more. Examples. 'any lambda equivalent to Lebesgue measure' is EGF.map_ac_of_equiv_addHaar on a finite-dimensional real vector space; nonsingularity needs no sigma-finiteness, and the theorem's sigma-finiteness comes from l.161. The manifold reading (the Lebesgue class in charts) and the Riemannian volume are not formalized (finding 2). Refutation EGF.printed_inflow_not_ac takes lambda = 1_[0,1) Leb and Phi(x) = x + 1. Then (Phi)_# lambda = 1_[1,2) Leb, which is not << lambda (EGF.not_map_ac_acMap), so the instance violates the new hypothesis and is no longer covered. That lambda is << Lebesgue but not equivalent to it, so the example clause does not reach it either. added_hypotheses = ['(Phi_i)_# lambda << lambda for each i'] appears at l.743, and nothing else was added.

At l.749-750, |J_s Phi_i^{-1}| becomes J^lambda_{Phi_i^{-1}}(s). l.752 defines J^lambda_{Phi_i^{-1}}(s) := d((Phi_i)_# lambda)/dlambda(s). That is literally the J of backward_policy_rnDeriv, (lam.map (Phi i)).rnDeriv lam. With it, f_in is inflowDensity, and beta^i is backwardWeight (term / f_in in ENNReal, then toReal). The direction is right: (Phi_i)_# Leb(A) = Leb(Phi_i^{-1} A) = int_A |det D Phi_i^{-1}|, so J^lambda is a Jacobian of Phi_i^{-1}, as coordJac (the fderiv of (Phi i).symm) has it. 'which is |det J_s Phi_i^{-1}| for Lebesgue (or Haar) measure' follows from EGF.map_eq_withDensity_abs_det: Phi_# mu = |det D(Phi^{-1})| mu for a Haar mu on a finite-dimensional real vector space and Phi^{-1} differentiable, so J^lambda = |det| mu-a.e. by rnDeriv_withDensity. The formula with |det| is the listed EGF.backward_policy_addHaar and _diffeomorph. 'the Riemannian Jacobian for the volume measure' is not formalized (finding 2). J^lambda is an a.e. class. A different version changes f_in and beta^i only on a lambda-null set, which is F_in-null, and IsBackwardPolicy does not see such a set. Refutation EGF.printed_backward_policy_false (lambda = lamCx, finite and equivalent to Lebesgue; translations; weights (2/3, 1/3) against the printed (1/2, 1/2)) is answered. On that same flow the lambda-Jacobian formula holds (EGF.cx_rnDeriv_reading, from backward_policy_rnDeriv with map_cxMap_ac). lamCx is not Haar, so the '|det| for Lebesgue (or Haar)' clause does not apply to it. The body's Eqs. (equ:tractable_inflow) and (equ:finstar) (l.227-237) are in the Lebesgue setting (l.226). They are correct there (backward_policy_addHaar, backward_policy_diffeomorph), so leaving them unchanged is what C-8 and the target's evidence say. added_hypotheses = [] and none was added.

l.754 reads: 'beta^i is defined F_in-a.e. (set to 0 where f_in(s) in {0, inf}); the backward policy is unique up to F_in-null sets, setwise: for each measurable X, every backward star policy agrees with B*(s -> X) for F_in-a.e. s'. Clause by clause. (i) The value 0: EGF.backwardWeight is (term / f_in).toReal in ENNReal. That is 0 where f_in = 0 (every term is <= f_in, and 0/0 = 0) and 0 where f_in = inf (x/inf = 0, and inf/inf = 0), as its docstring says. (ii) 'defined F_in-a.e.' means {f_in in {0, inf}} is F_in-null. This follows from conjunct 3 of backward_policy (sum beta^i = 1 F_in-a.e.), since every beta^i vanishes on that set. It also follows from conjunct 1 (F_in = f_in lambda) together with ae_inflowDensity_lt_top. (iii) Setwise uniqueness is conjunct 4 verbatim: for all B, IsBackwardPolicy B and X measurable imply B(.)(X) =ae[F_in] B*(.)(X). A 'backward star policy' is a kernel satisfying the relation F_in x B(Y -> X) = F_out x pi(X -> Y) of l.762, which is IsBackwardPolicy. Neither the TeX nor the Lean asks B to be finite. The setwise clause narrows the register's bare 'unique up to F_in-null sets' to exactly what the anchor states. Whole-kernel a.e. uniqueness (IsBackwardPolicy.ae_eq_posterior) needs a standard Borel space and a finite kernel B. It is true in the paper's Polish setting (l.161) for a finite B, but it is not an anchor and it is not needed. The hypotheses are those of C-7/C-8: backward_policy_rnDeriv is the J^lambda instance of backward_policy, so the anchor applies. Kind gap, so there is no refutation. added_hypotheses = [] and none was added.

findings.what: C-6: '... hence f_in exists (lambda being finite)'. The Lean needs only lambda sigma-finite (inflow_eq_withDensity_of_map_ac and backward_policy_rnDeriv take [SigmaFinite lam]). The sentence sits in the Tractability paragraph, which takes lambda to be Lebesgue on R^d (l.226), and that lambda is not finite. So the stated reason is false of the paragraph's own lambda, although the conclusion holds there because Lebesgue is sigma-finite. The parenthetical leans on l.161's standing finite lambda, which v1 itself already contradicts at l.155 and l.226. This is not an overclaim, since the conclusion is proved under a weaker hypothesis. It is a hypothesis stronger than the Lean needs, and in its paragraph it contradicts the stated lambda. It comes from C-6's corrected text.
findings.fix: TeX: '($\lambda$ being $\sigma$-finite)'. This is true for Lebesgue measure, for the Riemannian volume and for any finite lambda, and it is exactly the Lean hypothesis. Register: make the same change in C-6's `corrected`.

findings.what: C-6, C-7, C-8: three illustrative instances have no formal counterpart. They are '(true for diffeomorphisms and the Riemannian volume)' (l.232); '(for instance the Riemannian volume, or any lambda equivalent to Lebesgue measure)' (l.743), whose Euclidean case is EGF.map_ac_of_equiv_addHaar while the manifold case is not formalized; and 'the Riemannian Jacobian for the volume measure' (l.752). Mathlib at fabf563a has no manifold volume measure, as the SCOPE sections of EGF/BackwardPolicy.lean and EGF/InflowNonsingular.lean disclose. These are instances of the hypothesis (Phi_i)_# lambda << lambda, or identifications of J^lambda, not conclusions of any statement. Each is a standard fact: a C^1 diffeomorphism maps null sets to null sets in charts, and the density of the push-forward of the Riemannian volume is the Riemannian Jacobian (the change-of-variables formula). They are in the adopted corrected texts and in DEC-141's form of record ('which holds for diffeomorphisms and a smooth volume'). They are not an overclaim of any anchored statement and may stay, but nothing in the register records that they rest on an unformalized fact. Note also that 'For an EGF' (l.196, l.232) applies the nonsingular-moves theorem to the EGF of l.218 (a Riemannian manifold with its volume, and diffeomorphisms) through exactly this unformalized instance; only the Euclidean case (l.226's setting) is proved.
findings.fix: Register: in the `finding` of C-6, C-7 and C-8, record that the Riemannian-volume instances, and lambda equivalent to the Lebesgue class on a manifold, are standard facts not formalized at the pin. The Euclidean instances are EGF.map_ac_of_diffeomorph, EGF.map_ac_of_equiv_addHaar and EGF.map_eq_withDensity_abs_det. No TeX change is required. If the author prefers the body to lead with the proved case, l.232 could read '(true for diffeomorphisms and Lebesgue measure, as here, and for diffeomorphisms and the Riemannian volume)'.

answers.corrector_point_1: Yes, faithful to the entry and to the anchors. The entry's `printed` names both main.tex:196 and 231-234, and the moves do not exist yet at l.196, so a pointer there and the full sentence in Section 3 is the right split. The pointer and the sentence say together what the corrected sentence says. Making F_out << lambda explicit is right: it is `hout` in inflow_ac_of_map_ac, InflowAC.of_map_ac and inflow_eq_withDensity_of_map_ac. The paper already presupposes it through f_out (l.194, l.199, l.744), so it restricts nothing. (Phi_i)_# mu := mu(Phi_i^{-1}(.)) is Measure.map, so (Phi_i)_# lambda << lambda is `hPhi` literally, and it is defined before its uses at l.743 and l.752. Only the register's `corrected` text needs aligning (finding 4).
answers.corrector_point_2: Right call. The setwise clause is conjunct 4 of EGF.backward_policy (and of backward_policy_rnDeriv) verbatim, and it asks no finiteness of the competing kernel. The whole-kernel form, IsBackwardPolicy.ae_eq_posterior, needs StandardBorelSpace and IsFiniteKernel B. It would be true in the paper's Polish setting for a finite B, but it is not an anchor, and it would add 'finite' to 'every backward star policy'.
answers.corrector_point_3: They are claims beyond the Lean in the narrow sense: no declaration states them, and Mathlib at the pin has no manifold volume. They are instances of the stated hypothesis (Phi_i)_# lambda << lambda, or identifications of J^lambda, not conclusions of the theorem. Each is a standard fact, and each is in the adopted corrected texts and in DEC-141's form of record. So they are acceptable as illustrative examples and are not an overclaim; they need not be dropped. What is missing is a record: the register should say the Riemannian instances are unformalized standard facts and should list the Euclidean anchors (EGF.map_ac_of_diffeomorph, map_ac_of_equiv_addHaar, map_eq_withDensity_abs_det); see findings 2 and 3. Optional TeX for l.232, leading with the proved case of that paragraph: '(true for diffeomorphisms and Lebesgue measure, as here, and for diffeomorphisms and the Riemannian volume)'.
answers.corrector_point_4: It does not make the conclusion false: f_in exists there, because Lebesgue is sigma-finite and that is all inflow_eq_withDensity_of_map_ac needs. But the parenthetical gives 'lambda finite' as the reason inside a paragraph whose lambda is Lebesgue on R^d. So, read locally, it asserts something false of that lambda, leaning on l.161's standing assumption, which v1 already contradicts at l.155 and l.226. Write '($\lambda$ being $\sigma$-finite)', which is exactly the Lean hypothesis and true in every setting the paper names (finding 1).
answers.corrector_point_5: Yes. l.771 rests on (Phi_i)_# lambda = J^lambda lambda, which is Measure.withDensity_rnDeriv_eq under (Phi_i)_# lambda << lambda (l.743) with lambda sigma-finite (l.161) and (Phi_i)_# lambda sigma-finite (Phi_i a measurable embedding). That is precisely how backward_policy_rnDeriv discharges backward_policy's hJ before setLIntegral_egf_eq and lintegral_mul_jacobian carry out l.766-773. The rest of the deduction (l.775-782) is backward_policy conjuncts 1-2. The final 'The result follows' divides by f_in, which is where C-9's a.e. clause is needed, and it is there.
